Tract III and roads constructed around the coal handling facilities.

Haul roads have been constructed from the mining area to the coal handling facilities. Approximately 57 acres are involved in this road system. A 36-mile rail spur has been constructed from near the substation at Sanders to the present mine site.
As coal production increases upon Tracts II and III, traffic will increase dramatically on roads outside of the mine area. Such an increase in traffic will most likely stimulate the up-grading of the secondary County Highway 384 from the mine to Hardin. It has been indicated that an increase in traffic may also warrant improving the county road from the mine area north to Interstate 94. Upgrading local transportation systems might stimulate minimal commercial development, such as a cafe or filling station at selected locations. Market access for local ranchers would be improved by the new roads.
At the low level of development, it is assumed that a 4.5 mile haul road will be constructed from Tract II to the present coal handling facilities on Tract III. Some 136 acres of land will be required. At the high level of production a 3.5 mile railroad spur to Tract II would be required. This spur-would utilized some 212 acres for construction and right-of-way. A haul road 2.5 miles long would be required to haul mined coal to the coal handling facilities and railroad spur in Tract II.
Relocation of approximately 1.2 miles of county road in Tract II would occur as mining progresses.
